overview: An active day on bpf-next with 65 patches across 16 series. The standout contribution is a large 13-patch series from Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi adding arena argument support to kfuncs and struct_ops, enabling BPF programs to pass arena-tagged pointers directly to kernel functions with full x86 JIT support. Other notable work includes preemption-safety fixes for the BPF stack map code from Jiri Olsa, BTF declaration tag emission for kfuncs in resolve_btfids, and several verifier correctness and arena robustness fixes.

patches.title: bpf: Support __arena and __arena__nullable kfunc argument suffixes
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Adds support for __arena and __arena__nullable argument suffix annotations on kfunc parameters, allowing kfuncs to accept pointers into BPF arena memory regions. The verifier learns to recognize and validate these arena-tagged kfunc arguments, rebasing user-space arena pointers to their kernel-mapped equivalents before the call. This is the core verifier change in a 13-patch series (v4) that also adds JIT-level rebasing in the x86 backend and extends the same semantics to struct_ops method arguments. It enables a new class of kfuncs that operate on shared kernel/user arena memory without requiring explicit pointer conversion by the BPF program.

patches.title: resolve_btfids: Emit bpf_kfunc and bpf_fastcall decl tags
patches.author: Ihor Solodrai
patches.summary: Extends the resolve_btfids build tool to emit BTF declaration tags for functions annotated with __bpf_kfunc and __bpf_fastcall, making these compile-time annotations visible in the kernel's BTF image at runtime. This allows tools like libbpf and introspection utilities to discover kfunc properties directly from BTF rather than relying on kernel-internal flag tables. The broader 6-patch series (v2) also adds BTF deduplication after btf2btf transformations, handles KF_ARENA_* flags in resolve_btfids, and adds documentation for the new annotation emission mechanism.

patches.title: bpf: Track verifier instruction stats for each subprogram
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Introduces per-subprogram instruction counters in the BPF verifier so that veristat and the verifier log can show which subprograms individually dominate verification complexity, rather than only reporting a single total. The series (v6, 6 patches) also propagates async callback instruction counts to scheduling subprograms, improves the human-readable format of stack depth statistics, and adjusts veristat's stack depth parsing to match. These improvements make it significantly easier to diagnose and optimize programs with complex subprogram call graphs.

patches.title: bpf: Disable preemption in bpf_get_stackid
patches.author: Jiri Olsa
patches.summary: Fixes a latent preemption-safety issue in the bpf_get_stackid helper by wrapping the stack-walking path with preempt_disable/enable, preventing corruption of per-CPU buffers used by the stack map code if a preemption event occurs mid-walk. This is part of a large 12-patch series (v4) that first refactors __bpf_get_stackid into smaller, focused helper functions (stackid_init, stackid_fastpath, stackid_new_bucket, callchain_store, callchain_finalize) to make the preemption and callchain management logic easier to audit and modify. Companion patches also disable preemption in __bpf_get_stack and avoid mutating the callchain in the perf-event stack walk paths.

patches.title: bpf: Mark pending sub-register zero extension before pruning a state
patches.author: Daniel Borkmann
patches.summary: Fixes a verifier correctness bug where pending sub-register zero extension (zext) markers were not considered during state pruning, allowing the pruner to incorrectly merge a state that still has pending zext obligations with a previously cached state that does not. Without the fix, programs could be accepted with incorrect register values after the pruned-out state. The 4-patch series extends the same fix to cover arena pointer zero extensions and adds regression test cases for both scenarios in selftests.

patches.title: bpf: Add KF_SPINLOCK_SAFE flag for kfuncs under bpf_spin_lock
patches.author: Kaitao Cheng
patches.summary: Introduces a new KF_SPINLOCK_SAFE kfunc flag that marks individual kfuncs as safe to call while a BPF spin lock is held, lifting the previous blanket verifier rejection of all kfunc calls within spin-lock critical sections. The second patch in the 3-patch series (v2) annotates existing non-sleeping, lock-safe kfuncs with the new flag. A selftest verifies that module kfuncs correctly annotated with KF_SPINLOCK_SAFE can be invoked under a held spin lock without verifier rejection.

patches.title: bpf: Add a sleepable page allocator for map memory
patches.author: Jiayuan Chen
patches.summary: Adds a sleepable page allocator abstraction for BPF map memory to properly support cgroup memory limit (memory.max) reclaim and OOM killing during arena fault-in. Previously, arena page faults were handled while holding a lock, preventing the memory reclaim path from sleeping and causing unpredictable failures under memory pressure. The 4-patch series (v2) moves allocation outside the arena lock, adds a read_cgroup_file() helper to cgroup_helpers, and includes a selftest that exercises arena fault-in under a tight memory.max constraint.

patches.title: libbpf: support selective kernel module BTF loading via .kmod_btfs section
patches.author: Fuyu Zhao
patches.summary: Proposes (RFC) a mechanism for BPF programs to declare which kernel module BTFs they require via a new .kmod_btfs ELF section, enabling libbpf to skip iterating and loading all available kmod BTFs and instead load only those explicitly needed by the program. On systems with many kernel modules, loading all kmod BTFs at program load time is a measurable overhead; selective loading can significantly reduce BPF load latency. The companion patch adds selftests that verify correct behavior when only a subset of kmod BTFs is loaded.
